offence_severity: Minimum: Death (Section 302), Maximum: Life imprisonment (Section 302/34 IPC)
physical_harm: The deceased was brutally murdered, her body chopped into two pieces, and there were multiple ante-mortem and post-mortem injuries indicating severe physical harm.
number_of_offences: Four offences charged, three upheld (Manoj, Jamnadas, Dhanwantari), one acquitted (Vishal)
premeditation_planning: The court found that the appellants had common intention with the co-accused in the commission of the murder, indicating premeditation and planning.
key_evidence_accepted: The chain of circumstances proved on the record against the appellants, including the murder inside the house, the body being cut into two pieces and thrown in the park, blood stains found in the matrimonial house, and the false explanation given by the appellants under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, particularly PW 1 to PW 5 who saw the mother-in-law throwing the dead body in the park, and the medical experts who confirmed the homicidal nature of the injuries.

legal_representation.accused: Sushil Kumar Jain, Sr. Adv., Puneet Jain, Abhinav Gupta, Ms. Chhaya Kirti, Ms. Ankita Gupta, Ms. Pratibha Jain, P. K. Jain, Ad vs.
legal_representation.state: C. D. Singh, Sandeepan Pathak, Ms. Sylona Mohapatra, Ms. G Saumay Kalra, Advs.

investigation_status: Charge sheet filed against four accused; trial completed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the deceased was murdered inside the house of the appellants, her body was cut into two pieces and thrown in the park, and that the appellants had common intention with the co-accused in the commission of the brutal murder. The chain of circumstances proved on the record against the appellants is complete, and the defence version has been proved to be false, which is an additional link in the chain of circumstances.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the deceased had gone to her relatives' place and was missing, and that the appellants were in the shop at the time of the incident. They claimed that the deceased was not missing from the house after going to her relative's place.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that in a case of circumstantial evidence, the chain of circumstances must be fully established, consistent only with the hypothesis of the guilt of the accused, conclusive in nature and tendency, excluding every possible hypothesis except the one proved, and forming a complete chain of evidence that leaves no reasonable ground for the conclusion consistent with the innocence of the accused.
precedent_relied_upon: Sharad Birdhichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra (1984) 4 SCC 116; Trimukh Maroti Kirkan v. State of Maharashtra (2006) 10 SCC 681; Suresh and another v. State of Haryana (2015) 2 SCC 227; State of W.B. v. Mir Mohammad Omar and others (2000) 8 SCC 382; Nafendra Singh and another v. State of MP. (2004) 10 SCC 699
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the appellants were found guilty of murder with common intention, and the chain of circumstances proved against them was complete, leaving no reasonable ground for the conclusion consistent with their innocence.
